correctness.rationale: Exact nine-by-nine point–line incidence bijections are exhaustively enumerated (42). The relative permutation cycle criterion exactly identifies one alternating six/eight-cycle. All 861 unordered matching pairs and all 42 BFS sources are checked, and the six-cycle parity-sector hub structure is certified by its unique local decomposition. A second standalone LCF construction verifies the graph isomorphism and reproduces the state, edge and distance counts; both checkers passed.

evidence: Dyer–Jerrum–Müller, arXiv:1501.07725, Section 1.3: switch replaces two pairs, hence a four-cycle; Pappus girth is six.
Ito et al., arXiv:1907.01700, Section 1, establishes unrestricted alternating-cycle reachability; it does not specify a small bounded cycle length.
Bau–Henning, DOI:10.1016/S0012-365X(02)00519-8, abstract explicitly assumes plane cubic bipartite graphs.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The only general connectivity result for arbitrary alternating-cycle lengths does not imply connectivity at maximum length eight or exact state graph invariants. The earlier four-cycle model is edgeless here, while the 2003 plane-graph hypothesis excludes the nonplanar Pappus graph.

value.rationale: The first cycle-length allowance that connects all perfect matchings is a natural dynamical invariant. The theorem gives a sharp threshold, classifies the two parity-obstructed components as explicitly constructed hub-hexagon graphs and determines the octagon-only defects and all shortest distances, substantially beyond a matching count or elementary parity statement.
